findings.title: False finite-descent degree divisibility in the algebraic tower proof

locations.locator: Theorem 3.4.12 statement and hypotheses
Finite upper-extension case, after K₁=K₂∩L₁ is introduced

findings.precise_defect: For intersecting subfields, [K₂:K₂∩L₁] need not divide [K₂L₁:L₁], even when the latter degree is prime. The subsequent degree equality and minimal-polynomial calculations inherit this false premise.
findings.mathematical_evidence: Let a=∛2, ζ a primitive cube root of unity, K=Q, K₂=Q(a), L₁=Q(ζa), L₂=Q(a,ζ). Both cubic fields have degree3; they are distinct since K₂ is real and L₁ is not, hence their intersection is Q. Their compositum is L₂, of degree6 over Q, so [L₂:L₁]=2 while [K₂:K₂∩L₁]=3. All relevant source hypotheses hold, including a prime upper degree; use the usual adelic curve on Q. If the preceding degree equality were granted, the claimed irreducibility would follow, so this is not a second independent irreducibility counterexample.
findings.proposed_correction: Descend the finite upper extension and the finite data together to a sufficiently large finite base, preserving both total and separable degrees; then apply finite base change and extend cylinder identities by measure uniqueness.
findings.theorem_vs_proof_effect: The printed auxiliary claim is false and that proof step needs replacement. The tower theorem is not disproved. Current Lean implements the finite-descent repair.
findings.source_evidence: Original rendered manuscript pages read with AI vision by the assigned reviewers; not inferred from a transcription alone.
findings.legacy_disposition: Confirmed with the full source hypotheses; downstream irreducibility is not counted as an independent error.
findings.independent_adjudication: Confirmed by review-adjudicator; full adjudication recorded in the audit review checks.

findings.title: Cylinder sigma algebra need not equal Borel, even for a source adelic fibre

locations.locator: Section 3.1 definition: logarithmic measurability and integrability; properness is separate
Section 3.4.2 permits an arbitrary algebraic extension
Definition of A_{L,ω} as the smallest sigma algebra for finite restriction maps
Proof of Proposition 3.4.6, after the projective-limit topology is introduced

findings.precise_defect: The proof identifies the sigma algebra generated by finite projections with the full Borel sigma algebra of an arbitrary inverse limit. This fails without an additional hypothesis; a general cube objection alone would not establish failure in the specific adelic setting.
findings.mathematical_evidence: An actual source example realizes the cube. For uncountable I, take algebraically independent y_i over Q, x_i=y_i²−1, K=Q(x_i), L=Q(y_i). Give K the absolute value 2^(−ord_0), where ord_0 is minimum total degree, and use a one-point parameter space of mass1. Every nonzero log evaluation is an integrable finite constant, as required; properness and countability are not hypotheses here. Each sign vector ε defines an extension by total degree at y_i=ε_i. For finite J, E_J=K(y_j:j∈J) has degree2^|J| by sign automorphisms. Every extending absolute value is ultrametric, selects one sign for each j, and the binomial truncations of sqrt(1+x_j) show uniqueness for each sign: square-free basis elements are approximated by elements of K with error tending to zero. The E_J are cofinal among all finite stages. Thus the actual fibre is {±1}^I with its product topology and cylinder sigma algebra. Cylinder-measurable sets depend on countably many coordinates; a singleton is closed but not cylinder-measurable.
findings.proposed_correction: Delete the full-Borel identification and retain the specified cylinder sigma algebra, or impose a sufficient countable-cofinality hypothesis. The original proof already establishes a cylinder premeasure via compact clopen sets and applies Carathéodory; that route remains available.
findings.theorem_vs_proof_effect: The additional equality in the proof is false. The stated probability-on-cylinders conclusion is not refuted, nor is existence of a Borel extension disproved. Not every adelic fibre has unequal sigma algebras.
findings.source_evidence: Original rendered manuscript pages read with AI vision by the assigned reviewers; not inferred from a transcription alone.
findings.legacy_disposition: Strengthened from a general inverse-limit objection to a verified counterexample within the exact source hypotheses; attribution of the measure-construction route corrected.
findings.independent_adjudication: Confirmed by an independent review-adjudicator using a finite-basis approximation proof; not Lean-certified.

findings.title: Infinite archimedean mass leaves the Northcott coefficient bound non-finite

locations.locator: Start of Section 3.5: the adelic curve is proper
Definition 3.5.2 and Theorem 3.5.3 hypotheses
Lemma 3.5.5 first inequality; Claim 3.5.6 coefficient estimate and ensuing finitely-many-polynomials conclusion
End of the Northcott proof and Corollary 3.5.7

findings.precise_defect: The hypotheses do not ensure ν(Ω_∞)<∞. For infinite mass the displayed error is not a finite real expression. Under a nonnegative extended-real convention with 0·∞=0 the bound remains true, but for a positive logarithmic factor it yields +∞ and cannot justify finitely many possible coefficient vectors.
findings.mathematical_evidence: Take the usual rational places V and Ω=V×{1,2,...} with counting measure and absolute values |q|_{(v,n)}=|q|_v^(2^(−n)). Absolute logarithmic integrals converge, the product formula holds, and the height of a reduced a/b is log max(|a|,b), proving Northcott directly. Yet Ω_∞ has infinite mass, while A=∫κdν=Σ_n2^(−n)=1. Locally the convolution estimate has factor m^κ, giving the finite error log(m)A. This constant is preserved by algebraic extension and yields the finite minimal-polynomial coefficient bound d h(α)+(d−1)log(2)A. For F=G=X+1 the heights are0,0,log2; replacing infinite mass by the totalized real value0 would give the false inequality log2≤0, an encoding artifact rather than a refutation of the extended-real bound.
findings.proposed_correction: Use A=∫κdν, which is finite under the adelic integrability axiom, throughout the Northcott proof. Alternatively add finite archimedean mass as an explicit extra hypothesis to the weaker printed proof. For m=1 explain the constant-factor case and the 0·∞ convention.
findings.theorem_vs_proof_effect: The unrestricted finite-real reading of the displayed expression is ill-defined; its extended-real reading is true but can be useless. The later finiteness deduction has a genuine gap. The theorem and finite-extension corollary survive the sharper bound.
findings.source_evidence: Original rendered manuscript pages read with AI vision by the assigned reviewers; not inferred from a transcription alone.
findings.legacy_disposition: New detailed review of Sections 3.5–3.7; separates an extended-real convention from the later finite-bound requirement.
